issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Milkable.messageOnMilk() should return a String (and the task text describes returning the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). However, the solution implementation defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a boolean and the Goat/Seal implementations print the milk message and return true. This return-type mismatch contradicts the specification and will confuse students implementing the interface and using it (e.g., Main prints m.messageOnMilk() expecting a message).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API with the problem statement: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String. Update Goat and Seal to return the milk message string ("[Animal Type] [name] is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Ensure callers (e.g., Main and any tests) print the returned String. This preserves the intended exercise of returning and using a message string.

issues.description: The method messageOnMilk() is specified in the problem statement and UML to return a String (the textual message "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), and the sample Main prints its return value. In the provided solution, Milkable.messageOnMilk() is declared to return boolean and Goat/Seal implementations print the message to stdout and return true. This mismatch in the expected return type and observable behavior will confuse students mapping the specification to the implementation and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API with the problem statement: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String, and update Goat and Seal to return the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (do not print inside the method). Adjust any call sites (e.g., Main and tests) to print the returned String.
